symptom: On Windows, `mxcli run --local --detach` opens a visible console window for every console program the detached run starts (java, mxbuild, gradle); several terminal windows pop up during a boot. The same run without `--detach`, as a background child of a shell, shows none
cause: `setDetachAttrs` started the run with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS`. DETACHED_PROCESS gives the run no console at all, so Windows allocates a new console, with its own window, for each console child the run starts
insight: A process with no console is not a quiet process: every console child it starts gets a NEW visible console. What silences a tree is one console that has no window, shared by all of it. CREATE_NO_WINDOW gives the run exactly that, and its children inherit it. Windows ignores CREATE_NO_WINDOW when it is combined with DETACHED_PROCESS, so the flag cannot simply be added to the old set. `HideWindow` does not help: it hides the run's own window only, not those of its children. Prove it by the mechanism, not the flag: a helper started through `setDetachAttrs` reports `GetConsoleCP` (0 = no console), `GetConsoleWindow` and `GetConsoleProcessList`; a console child of the helper must appear in the run's own process list and have no window. Before the fix the helper had no console and its child was alone on a visible window; after, the child shares the run's console, which has no window. Real run on Mendix 11.12.5 (Windows Terminal as the default terminal host): v0.26.0 showed 4 new visible windows during a boot, the fix 0, in two runs. A hidden console does not make a `conhost.exe` disappear (the run owns one), so count windows, not conhost processes. The run no longer shares the caller's console, so closing the launching terminal does not touch it, and `run stop` (`taskkill /T /F`) is unaffected
